requirement:
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
rationale:
I judge the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. I did not request any implementation source. Each obligation below maps to marked tests that assert the outcome.

**Mandatory inputs are recorded.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` runs a full authoring session in six determination and verbosity variants.
  - It asserts the evidence record contains a requirements input for the subject, a definition input for `terms.readiness`, and outline inputs for `src/lib.rs`.
  - It asserts outline inputs carry exactly `file`, `hash` and `item`, and that the record has exactly the schema's fields.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts the `fn[ready_test]` outline input and the `terms.readiness` definition input are in the evidence.
  - It also runs `validate_repository` on the harness-written evidence and finds no error for it. This shows the harness created records that ordinary evidence validation accepts.
  - A tampered record, with `determination` set to false, is rejected, so the check is not vacuous.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[implementation_discovery_has_no_text_or_evidence_until_the_model_requests_a_read]` shows the implementation `fn[ready]` is recorded only after the model reads it, and exactly once. A `references` discovery call is not recorded.

**Additional reads are recorded in the evidence input formats.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` covers item reads and line-range reads.
  - Item reads and line-range reads that reach end of file record outline inputs, and the terms they use are recorded as definition inputs.
  - Re-recording a read does not duplicate it.
  - A directory listing records nothing.
  - Failed or malformed reads are errors.
  - The recorded outline input equals `outline_input(...)`, with only file, selector and hash.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` asserts the recorded outline inputs are the innermost covering nodes. They have no text or line numbers, and nested selectors such as `mod[inner]/fn[second]` are recorded correctly.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` covers the requirements-form and definition-form reads.
  - The `requirements` input carries `requirements`, `matches` and `text`. The `definition` input carries `definition` and `text`.
  - The definitions those reads depend on are recorded with them.
  - Recording the same read twice leaves one set of inputs, equal to the delivered inputs.

**Selected search dependencies are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#fn[selected_dependencies_keep_the_delivered_hash_and_accumulate_without_reads]` covers search selection.
  - Only the tags named in `used` are recorded, with the hash from delivery time rather than a later edit.
  - Duplicate tags and repeated finishes do not duplicate inputs.
  - An empty `used` list records nothing.
  - A later read of the same item is also deduplicated.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[a_helper_used_only_through_a_search_snippet_invalidates_saved_evidence_when_weakened]` runs end to end. A helper is recorded only through a search snippet, with no `habeas` call. Its input carries no text and validates as fresh. It then fails validation with a hash error after the helper is weakened, and the unrelated function is not recorded.

**Only supplied sources are recorded.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[only_inputs_on_delivered_pages_are_recorded]` shows that on a paged result, only the entries on delivered pages become inputs.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` shows each page's delivery equals its own inputs plus definitions.

The remaining marked tests, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` and `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]`, add checks that the lines read appear as outline inputs and that a model read produces an outline input without text.

I found no gap in the three kinds of source or the three input formats.

text: :::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs, additional reads, and selected search dependencies under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs`, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} finish_search.inputs
For each tag selected by a valid `finish_search` call, the harness MUST record
its `file`, `item`, and structural hash as an outline input under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` before acknowledging that call.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
